rows.jp: がくん、と体が突き押された気分だった。
rows.en: My body lurched as if someone had shoved me.

ghs.en: Twang, then the feeling of my body being pushed through.
ghs.assessment: がくん is a sudden jolt or lurch, not the sound 'twang,' and 突き押された describes the body feeling abruptly shoved, not pushed through something.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With a jolt, it felt as though my body had been shoved.'

highlights.text: Twang, then the feeling of my body being pushed through.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...ngh."

rows.jp: そうか。と思った。
rows.en: So that was it, I thought.

ghs.en: Of course. I thought.

rows.jp: 妙に納得してしまった。
rows.en: It made a peculiar kind of sense.

ghs.en: Oddly I have completely understood.

rows.jp: 自分の胸を貫く、一本の矢。
rows.en: An arrow piercing my chest.

ghs.en: A single bolt was piercing my chest.
ghs.assessment: 矢 is an arrow. 'Bolt' substitutes crossbow-specific ammunition not named by this line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A single arrow pierced my chest.'

highlights.text: A single bolt was piercing my chest.

rows.jp: そうか。
rows.en: I see.

ghs.en: Of course.

rows.jp: そうかそうか。
rows.en: I see, I see.

ghs.en: Of course of course.

rows.jp: きっと俺は動いてしまったのだ。
rows.en: I must have moved.

ghs.en: I have definitely moved, indeed,
ghs.assessment: きっと...してしまった is a retrospective inference: 'I must have moved.' The present-perfect 'have definitely moved, indeed' is stilted and changes inference into emphatic certainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I must have moved.'

highlights.text: I have definitely moved, indeed,

rows.jp: そして霧に撃たれた。
rows.en: And Kiri shot me.

ghs.en: and then I was shot by Kiri.

rows.jp: 実にわかりやすい。
rows.en: Perfectly straightforward.

ghs.en: Truly easy to understand.

rows.jp: 誰だろう。
rows.en: Who was that?

ghs.en: Who's even that.
ghs.assessment: 誰だろう is the narrator wondering who the voice belongs to. 'Who's even that' is not idiomatic for an unidentified speaker.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Who could it be?'

highlights.text: Who's even that.

rows.jp: 誰が心配してくれているのかな？
rows.en: Who could be worried about me?

ghs.en: Is somebody even worrying about me?

rows.jp: 先輩かな。
rows.en: Maybe Miyasumi.

ghs.en: Senpai maybe?

rows.jp: 冬子かな。
rows.en: Maybe Touko.

ghs.en: Touko maybe?

rows.jp: 美希かな。
rows.en: Maybe Miki.

ghs.en: Miki maybe?

rows.jp: 桜庭か友貴だったら……切ないなぁ。
rows.en: If it was Sakuraba or Tomoki... what a letdown.

ghs.en: If it's Sakuraba or Tomoki... that'd huuurt.

rows.jp: すまん。俺死ぬわ。
rows.en: Sorry. Guess I’m dying.

ghs.en: Sorry. Me die now.
ghs.assessment: The source is blunt but grammatical: 'Sorry. I'm going to die.' 'Me die now' invents broken pidgin syntax not licensed by the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sorry. I'm going to die.'

highlights.text: Sorry. Me die now.

rows.jp: 桃園の誓い……守れなかった……。
rows.en: The Oath of the Peach Garden... I couldn’t keep it...

ghs.en: I could not uphold... the Oath of the Peach Garden...

rows.jp: って、もともと破っていたんだっけ。
rows.en: Wait, hadn’t I broken that already?

ghs.en: Wait, I broke that from the start haven't I.
ghs.assessment: The source corrects the preceding thought by recalling that the oath had already been broken. The English uses a simple past and malformed tag question.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait, hadn't I already broken it from the start?'

highlights.text: Wait, I broke that from the start haven't I.

rows.jp: ははは。
rows.en: Ha ha ha.

ghs.en: Hahahah.

rows.jp: はははは。
rows.en: Ha ha ha ha.

ghs.en: Hahahahah.

rows.jp: 笑いたくても声が出ない。
rows.en: I wanted to laugh, but no sound came out.

ghs.en: I wanna laugh but no voice comes out.

rows.jp: 胸のあたりから、もやもやした圧迫感がこみあげてくる。
rows.en: A dull pressure rose from somewhere in my chest.

ghs.en: From the center of my chest, a foggy oppressive sensation fills my heart.
ghs.assessment: The source says a hazy pressure wells up from around the chest. 'Fills my heart' adds a distinct internal destination and uses 'foggy oppressive sensation' as an awkward physical description.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A hazy pressure wells up from around my chest.'

highlights.text: From the center of my chest, a foggy oppressive sensation fills my heart.

rows.jp: 胸元を見ると、自分の吐いた血が足下まで濡らしていた。
rows.en: I looked down. The blood I’d coughed up had soaked me all the way to my feet.

ghs.en: On looking at the pit of my stomach, the blood I've spilled dampens me down to my feet.
ghs.assessment: 胸元 is the chest, not the pit of the stomach, and 吐いた血 is blood coughed or vomited up, not merely blood 'spilled.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I look at my chest, the blood I coughed up has soaked me all the way to my feet.'

highlights.text: On looking at the pit of my stomach, the blood I've spilled dampens me down to my feet.

rows.jp: こりゃ大事だ。
rows.en: Well, this was serious.

ghs.en: Maaan this is trouble.

rows.jp: やばい、マジで死ぬ。
rows.en: Oh, shit. I’m really going to die.

ghs.en: This looks very bolt, I'll die for real.
ghs.assessment: 'This looks very bolt' is nonsensical English and introduces 'bolt,' which has no counterpart in the Japanese sentence. The source simply says the situation is bad and death is imminent.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This is bad. I'm really going to die.'

highlights.text: This looks very bolt, I'll die for real.

rows.jp: 死にたくないなぁ。
rows.en: I don’t want to die.

ghs.en: But I don't wanna die!

rows.jp: すごくすごく生きたいぞ。
rows.en: I want to live. So, so badly.

ghs.en: I wanna live so so very much!

rows.jp: たくさんＨなこともしたいし、テレビも見たいし、連載もののマンガだってちゃんと結末を見ておきたいし。
rows.en: I still want to have tons of sex, watch TV, and see how all my serialized manga end.

ghs.en: And I wanna do lots of pervy things, and I wanna watch the TV, and I wanna see a real conclusion to manga serials.
ghs.assessment: English does not normally use 'the TV' for the activity of watching television, and ちゃんと結末を見ておきたい means wanting to see how serialized manga end, not to see a 'real conclusion.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I want to do lots of dirty things, watch TV, and find out how all the manga I'm following end.'

highlights.text: And I wanna do lots of pervy things, and I wanna watch the TV, and I wanna see a real conclusion to manga serials.

rows.jp: やだなぁ、死ぬの。
rows.en: I really don’t want to die.

ghs.en: Not nice, huh, getting the shaft and dying.
ghs.assessment: やだなぁ、死ぬの is simply the aversion 'I don't want to die.' 'Getting the shaft' invents an unrelated idiom and changes the thought into a complaint about unfair treatment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I really don't want to die.'

highlights.text: Not nice, huh, getting the shaft and dying.

rows.jp: あー、でも俺ってヤングアダルト候補生だからなんか奇蹟の力で生き返るかな。
rows.en: Then again, I’m a young-adult-in-training. Maybe some miraculous power will bring me back.

ghs.en: Ahhh, but me's a Young Adult Cadet so I'll just come back to life by the power of a miracle or something won't I.
ghs.assessment: The casual Japanese remains grammatical. 'Me's a ... Cadet' and the stacked future and tag-question syntax manufacture a broken comic dialect that the source does not contain.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah, but I'm a young-adult candidate, so maybe some miraculous power will bring me back to life.'

highlights.text: Ahhh, but me's a Young Adult Cadet so I'll just come back to life by the power of a miracle or something won't I.

rows.jp: 俺の亡骸に美少女がすがりついて涙を落とすと、その雫が触れた瞬間パーッと明るく輝いてたちまち蘇生したりするのだ。
rows.en: A beautiful girl would throw herself over my corpse and weep. The moment one of her tears touched me, I’d blaze with light and spring back to life.

ghs.en: My spoils shall be hugged and cried upon by a beautiful girl, and the instant one of her tear touches me, boom!, a brilliant white light and suddenly I will be revived.
ghs.assessment: 亡骸 means the narrator's corpse or remains, not his 'spoils.' The English also misuses the singular in 'one of her tear' and obscures the causal sequence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A beautiful girl will cling to my corpse and weep; the instant one of her tears touches me, a brilliant light will flare and I will spring back to life.'

highlights.text: My spoils shall be hugged and cried upon by a beautiful girl, and the instant one of her tear touches me, boom!, a brilliant white light and suddenly I will be revived.

rows.jp: 感動だね。
rows.en: How touching.

ghs.en: So emotional innit.
ghs.assessment: 感動だね calls the imagined scene moving or touching. 'So emotional innit' substitutes an unsupported dialect tag and describes emotionality rather than the response it produces.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How moving.'

highlights.text: So emotional innit.

rows.jp: じゃ、とりあえず死に際に何かギャグをかましてみようかな。
rows.en: Maybe I should try one last joke before I die.

ghs.en: So, for now, what sketch should I force myself into here on the edge of death?
ghs.assessment: The narrator considers pulling a gag at the moment of death. 'What sketch should I force myself into' changes a joke he performs into a sketch imposed on himself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'For now, maybe I should try one last gag as I die.'

highlights.text: So, for now, what sketch should I force myself into here on the edge of death?

rows.jp: 男としてそれは格好いいことだ。
rows.en: A man could hardly ask for a cooler way to go.

ghs.en: That's the cool thing for a man to do.

rows.jp: 喋れないし、身動きがほとんど取れないから……あまり派手なことはできない。
rows.en: I can’t speak, and I can barely move... so nothing too elaborate.

ghs.en: Because I can't talk, and I can't take much in the way of movements... I can't do anything particularly flashy.
ghs.assessment: 身動きがほとんど取れない means that he can barely move. 'Can't take much in the way of movements' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't speak and can barely move, so I can't do anything very flashy.'

highlights.text: Because I can't talk, and I can't take much in the way of movements... I can't do anything particularly flashy.

rows.jp: って、何もできねぇよ。
rows.en: Wait. I can’t do anything.

ghs.en: Wait, then I can't do nuthin'!

rows.jp: うわー、このまま死ぬのか！　いやじゃー！
rows.en: Oh, God, am I really going to die like this?! No! I don’t want to!

ghs.en: Bwaaah, do I just have die like this! That's waaay bad!
ghs.assessment: 'Do I just have die' is missing 'to,' while いやじゃ is 'I don't want to,' not the evaluative 'that's bad.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Am I going to die like this? I don't want to!'

highlights.text: Bwaaah, do I just have die like this! That's waaay bad!

rows.jp: 誰か俺の頭に金ダライを落としてくれーっ！
rows.en: Somebody drop an anvil on my head!

ghs.en: Someone make a metal pan fall on my heeead!
ghs.assessment: 金ダライ is the metal washbasin used as a stock slapstick prop, not a generic cooking pan. The object is part of the requested gag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Somebody drop a metal washbasin on my head!'

highlights.text: Someone make a metal pan fall on my heeead!

rows.jp: 俺に笑いを、笑いをくれ！
rows.en: Give me a laugh! One last laugh!

ghs.en: Laugh, please, laugh at me!
ghs.assessment: 俺に笑いを means 'give me laughter/a laugh.' 'Laugh at me' instead commands others to make the narrator the object of ridicule.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Give me a laugh—give me laughter!'

highlights.text: Laugh, please, laugh at me!

rows.jp: どわあ、血がひどいな！
rows.en: Whoa, that’s a lot of blood!

ghs.en: D'wah, blood's nasty innit!
ghs.assessment: 血がひどい comments on the severity or amount of blood. 'Blood's nasty innit' changes the observation into a judgment of disgust and adds an unsupported dialect tag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Whoa, that's a lot of blood!'

highlights.text: D'wah, blood's nasty innit!

rows.jp: さっきより広がってるぞ。一面血だらけだ。
rows.en: It’s spreading. Blood everywhere.

ghs.en: It's spread lots more than before. I'm just one big stain of blood now.
ghs.assessment: 一面血だらけ says blood covers the whole area. 'I'm just one big stain of blood' turns the narrator himself into the stain.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It has spread farther than before. There's blood everywhere.'

highlights.text: It's spread lots more than before. I'm just one big stain of blood now.

rows.jp: 人間ひとりからこんな血が流れるのか……奥が深いな。
rows.en: Who knew one guy could bleed this much...? Deep stuff.

ghs.en: Can all this blood be spilled from a human being alone? ...this one's deep.

rows.jp: まっかだ。
rows.en: Bright red.

ghs.en: It's all red.

rows.jp: 色がわかるってことは、俺は俺のままなんだな。
rows.en: If I can see color, I must still be myself.

ghs.en: I can recognize the color, meaning I still gotta be as I am.

rows.jp: ギリギリで『戻った』のか。
rows.en: Did I “come back” at the last possible moment?

ghs.en: Have I Returned at this very last moment?

rows.jp: うむ。
rows.en: Indeed.

ghs.en: Mh-hm.

rows.jp: いいことだ。
rows.en: Good.

ghs.en: That'd be nice.
ghs.assessment: いいことだ is a present judgment that this is good. 'That'd be nice' makes it a conditional wish.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's good.'

highlights.text: That'd be nice.

rows.jp: 不意に、首から上の感覚が戻った。
rows.en: Suddenly, I could feel everything from the neck up again.

ghs.en: Unexpectedly, the feeling returns from the neck up.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese narrates a completed return of sensation in the past. The English abruptly switches to present tense.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Unexpectedly, feeling returned above my neck.'

highlights.text: Unexpectedly, the feeling returns from the neck up.

rows.jp: 一時的なものだろう。
rows.en: Probably only temporary.

ghs.en: It's gotta be temporary.

rows.jp: ショック状態から各部の筋肉が回復しているんだ。
rows.en: My muscles must be recovering from the shock.

ghs.en: Muscles all around have recovered from this state of shock.
ghs.assessment: The muscles are recovering as the body comes out of shock. 'Have recovered from this state of shock' treats the muscles themselves as the entity that suffered and completed recovery from the whole state.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The muscles throughout my body are recovering as I come out of shock.'

highlights.text: Muscles all around have recovered from this state of shock.

rows.jp: ……といっても、そんな保たないだろう。
rows.en: ...Not that it’ll last long.

ghs.en: ...but I have to add, that's not likely to last.

rows.jp: もう意識がもうろうとしている。
rows.en: My mind is already growing hazy.

ghs.en: Awareness has already grown indistinct,

rows.jp: 呼吸も不自然に浅く細かい。
rows.en: My breathing is unnaturally quick and shallow.

ghs.en: breathing is unnaturally shallow and elaborate as well.
ghs.assessment: 細かい describes breathing as quick or rapid. 'Elaborate' means complex or detailed and is not a property of the distressed breathing described here.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My breathing is unnaturally shallow and rapid.'

highlights.text: breathing is unnaturally shallow and elaborate as well.

rows.jp: 苦しささえわからない。
rows.en: I can’t even feel the pain anymore.

ghs.en: I can't even tell if I'm in pain.

rows.jp: 見あげた先。
rows.en: Above me...

ghs.en: I looked up and, ahead,

rows.jp: 赤はどこまでも広がっていた。
rows.en: The red went on forever.

ghs.en: the red had been spreading, everywhere, anywhere.
ghs.assessment: The source says the red had spread without limit. 'Had been spreading, everywhere, anywhere' is an ungrammatical sequence of adverbs and changes the completed visual state into an ongoing process.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Red had spread as far as I could see.'

highlights.text: the red had been spreading, everywhere, anywhere.

rows.jp: ……やると思った。
rows.en: ...I knew it.

ghs.en: ....it's done, I thought.
ghs.assessment: やると思った means 'I knew [the actor] would do it' or 'I thought [the actor] might,' depending on the carried subject. 'It's done' replaces that prospective judgment with a completed passive result.
ghs.remedy: Use the contextually bound subject in a prospective line such as 'I knew they would do it.'

highlights.text: ....it's done, I thought.

rows.jp: その瞬間、俺は死んだ。
rows.en: At that moment, I died.

ghs.en: That instant I died.
